narrative:

This high probability indicates that, based on historical data from similar students, the likelihood of you not passing the exam is considerably elevated.

The most critical factors contributing to this prediction were your academic performance in your first and third years, as well as your work status. Your grades placed you in the lowest decile compared to accepted students, who generally performed much better academically. This suggests that your academic foundation may not be strong enough to handle the rigorous demands of law school and the bar exam.

Additionally, your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 is notably below the average of 3.23 among accepted students. This lower GPA raises concerns about your preparedness for the challenges of law school, which is a significant predictor of bar exam success. 

Lastly, your decision to work part-time while studying may also have played a role. Most successful applicants are able to commit fully to their studies, which can be crucial for mastering the material needed for the bar exam.

Moving forward, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance, perhaps by seeking additional support or resources to strengthen your study habits. Additionally, consider dedicating more time to your studies to enhance your understanding of the material, which could better prepare you for future applications.
